edges.description: Repeated conjunctival infection produces chronic keratoconjunctivitis, including active trachoma.
Cumulative inflammatory episodes leave clinically significant conjunctival scarring.
Eyelid scarring turns the eyelashes inward onto the globe.
In-turned eyelashes scratch the cornea, which predisposes to corneal opacity.
Corneal opacity from lash trauma leads to vision impairment and blindness.

nodes.description: Antibiotic mass drug administration reduces infection prevalence and transmission.

evidence.snippet: Surgery is offered to individuals with trichiasis and antibiotic mass drug administration and interventions to stimulate facial cleanliness and environmental improvement are designed to reduce infection prevalence and transmission.
Trachoma is a neglected tropical disease caused by infection with conjunctival strains of Chlamydia trachomatis. It can result in blindness.

nodes.description: Rounds of severe conjunctival inflammation are the step that precedes eyelid scarring.

evidence.snippet: Rounds of severe conjunctival inflammation lead to scarring of the eyelid
eyelashes predisposes to corneal opacity, vision impairment and blindness

nodes.description: Scarring of the eyelid marks the start of the second, non-communicable disease phase.

evidence.snippet: Rounds of severe conjunctival inflammation lead to scarring of the eyelid

nodes.description: Repeated conjunctival infection with C. trachomatis in childhood is the initiating step; it drives the chronic inflammation and eyelid scarring described in the downstream nodes.

evidence.snippet: Trachoma is a disease complex composed of two linked chronic processes: a recurrent, generally subclinical infectious-inflammatory disease that mostly affects children, and a non-communicable, cicatricial and, owing to trichiasis, eventually blinding disease
This scarring can cause inward rotation of the eyelashes so that they come into contact with the eyeball
